sections.overview: Evergestis limbata is a crambid moth in the genus Evergestis; its English species accounts call it the Border-striped Pearl.
sections.identification: The forewings show pale ground color with dark transverse markings; the adult is a small crambid moth.
sections.habitat: Regional British records place it in a range of habitats, though it is generally encountered singly or sparingly.
sections.diet: The caterpillar feeds on Brassicaceae, especially garlic mustard (Alliaria petiolata) and hedge mustard (Sisymbrium officinale).
sections.behavior: Adults are nocturnal moths recorded at light; the larva is seldom found despite reported host plants.
sections.reproduction: Available British records place adult flight in summer; the sources consulted give little species-specific detail on mating or egg laying.
sections.ecology: Compare Evergestis pallidata: both are brassica-feeding crambids, but pallidata has a distinct pale-and-brown wing pattern and its own host records.
sections.conservation: The British regional accounts describe local occurrence but do not supply a global conservation assessment.
